subject.title: Ensure transcript-to-client delivery consistency for channel-scoped sessions

question: What durable delivery-state contract should OpenClaw add for channel-scoped transcript entries: a transcript-entry ledger, an extension of delivery_queue_entries, or a different session-state projection?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but the durable schema, adapter reconciliation contract, idempotent redelivery policy, and UI/API shape cross persisted-state and channel compatibility boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design Generic Ledger First
options.body: Add a SQLite-backed transcript delivery ledger tied to outbound receipts and adapter reconciliation, then surface per-entry status in session APIs and Control UI.

options.title: Limit To Queue Mitigations
options.body: Keep accepting narrow recovery mitigations while leaving this issue open until maintainers are ready to commit to the broader delivery-state surface.

options.title: Split Runtime And UI Work
options.body: Track runtime ledger/reconciler design separately from Control UI surfacing if the full implementation is too large for one lane.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Ledger First
recommendation.body: Add a SQLite-backed transcript delivery ledger tied to outbound receipts and adapter reconciliation, then surface per-entry status in session APIs and Control UI.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing candidate from durable outbound, queue storage, recovery, and SQLite state history.
